title: Compass Riff — Feedback sprint notes & micro-probes
body:
Purpose: rapid capture + synthesis from the last two weeks of field threads (topline customers, pilot accounts, forum posts). This is a working artifact intended to seed 2-week micro-probes and a prioritized patch list for eng/Product.

Executive TL;DR:
- Main signal: three clusters dominate our inbound: 1) KV-cache cold-starts and anomalous cost spikes, 2) unpredictable latency spikes on long-context prompts, 3) embedding/semantic-search mismatches for short queries.
- Quick wins (low effort): evict cache hints, improved error messaging on model fallbacks, conservative batch-size default for mixed-length workloads.
- Suggested next step: run 2-week micro-probe sprint tracking impact on latency percentiles and per-token spend for 5 pilot customers.

Data snapshot (qualitative + counts):
- Sources: CS tickets (34), Field interviews (6 calls), Forum threads (12), Onboarding logs (10k requests sampled).
- Most common phrases seen in logs: "sudden token bill", "inconsistent response quality", "chat reverted to shorter answers", "time to first token increased".

Customer quotes (verbatim, redacted):
- "We saw our token cost jump 3x overnight when a single endpoint switched models mid-rollout — need alerting at the account level." (Enterprise fintech)
- "The assistant repeats itself with long conversations; the engineer in our team suspects kv cache dying every 20–30 requests." (AI startup)
- "Short search queries return poor embeddings and we get noisy reranks even with same index." (e-commerce platform)

Cluster A — KV cache & cold-start behavior
- Symptom: intermittent regressions where prefix cache isn't reused; customers observe higher per-token compute and stale latencies.
- Frequency: ~40% of technical tickets in sampled week.
- Hypothesis: under certain autoscaling events we reinitialize runtime without warming cached KV slots; eviction/compaction policy too aggressive for mixed bursty traffic.
- Impact: high cost (per-token), UX regression (longer TTF), intermittent quality dips.
- Proposed micro-probe (owner: Ethan Park): instrument a lightweight metric tag (cache-warm=true/false) at route level for 2 weeks; expose a per-account cache-warmness dashboard. JIRA: JIRA-8932.
- Low-effort patch: add a best-effort warmup step during pool-scale-up (place-holder warm KV for common prefix sizes) — spike lab to estimate latency overhead.

Cluster B — Latency spikes for long contexts
- Symptom: p95/p99 spikes when seq length > 1024; some customers see time to first token (TT1) increase by 1.8x.
- Root causes suspected: kernel selection sometimes picks slower matmul kernel for longer seq; batching logic groups long and short requests causing head-of-line blocking.
- Impact: SLA violations for latency-sensitive tenants, engineering workarounds (sharding requests) causing increased client complexity.
- Proposed probes:
  1) Smart-binning for batching: segregate long-context requests to separate lanes with constrained batch sizes (owner: Maya Chen). Small experiment on dedicated dev cluster, measure p95.
  2) Kernel telemetry: record kernel decisions and correlate to sequence-length and device type; run a retrospective to improve selector heuristics.
- Quick mitigation: add a configuration toggle on routes to pin conservative kernel selection for long sequences until probe results.

Cluster C — Embedding quality & rerank mismatch
- Symptom: short queries (2–4 tokens) produce embeddings that rank irrelevant docs higher vs previous baseline.
- Observations: correlated with a recent model patch and a default embedding normalizer change rolled out to hosted catalog.
- Customer impact: feature regressions in search and reduced CTR for recommendations (reported by 4 customers).
- Action items: revert embedding normalizer for affected model family in hosted catalog (controlled rollback) and run A/B across 3 customers; gather quantitative vector-similarity deltas.

Priority table (with simple scoring):
- KV cache warmness: priority = high; effort = medium; quick-win potential = medium-high.
- Batching long contexts: priority = high; effort = medium; quick-win = medium.
- Embedding normalizer rollback: priority = medium; effort = low; quick-win = high.
- Better fallback messaging & audit trail: priority = medium; effort = low; quick-win = medium.

Micro-fixes we can ship in 1 sprint (week or less):
- Add per-route hints in Console: "expected cache-warm behavior" and expose recent scale events. (owner: Liam O'Connor) — PR: github/prs/342
- Add alert template for sudden per-account token-spend increases (>2x day-over-day) (owner: Sofia Alvarez) — ask Observability to roll into default alert set.
- Improve model-fallback user message: include which model variant was chosen and why (owner: Maya Chen).

Open questions & unknowns:
- How often are cache cold-starts triggered by infra autoscaling vs user-driven model switch? Need richer correlation telemetry.
- Are certain customer workloads (embedding-heavy vs chat-heavy) more affected by the default eviction policy? (sampling required)
- What is the unit-cost delta if we do best-effort warmups on scale-up (estimate before running probe)?

Measurement plan (2-week sprint):
- Metrics to capture: per-account p50/p95/p99 latency; per-account per-token compute cost; cache-warmness rate; kernel-selection events; embedding-similarity drift for control queries.
- Success criteria: reduce p99 latency for long-context lanes by 20% for pilot customers, reduce account-level unexplained token-cost spikes by 50%.

Next steps (concrete owners):
- Ethan: instrument cache-warm tag + dashboard (2 days to prototype) -> JIRA-8932.
- Maya: run smart-binning experiment on dev cluster (3 days setup, 7 days run). Measure p95.
- Liam: Console hint and scale-event surface (1 sprint). PR link above.
- Sofia: coordinate pilot customers for A/B (reach out to 5 pilot accounts; prepare communications).

Appendix — quick examples from logs (redacted):
- ticket#124512: "billing spike linked to endpoint prod-search-01 on 2026-02-03 03:42 UTC when scaleup occurred".
- slack thread #ops-alarms: "noticed repeated missing cache-warm flag during morning burst".

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Consider a low-cost synthetic 'warm' request on new GPU pool attach — may trade tiny compute for big downstream cost savings.
- If kernel selector improvements are non-trivial, fallback: expose a route-level knob for "latency-priority" vs "cost-priority".

If you have additional field snippets or logs, drop them into the "compass-riff-attachments" folder and ping here; I will fold into the next pass. This doc will be iterated after the first round of micro-probe data (target: 2026-03-15 for probe readout).
